title: Where do discounted properties come from, and which are real deals?
excerpt: A slow-selling project passes from the developer's own promotions to agents, then to group-buying clubs, and sometimes to auction. Sean traces the path, and what each discount really means.

question.context: Viewers were sending Sean properties with big advertised discounts and asking which to buy. He noticed most came through the same few channels.
question.text: Where can buyers find discounted property, and how genuine are the discounts?

answer.quote: you are the buyer you have the power
answer.summary: Discounts follow a project's struggle to sell: developer promotions, then agents, then group-buying clubs, and finally auctions. Many early discounts are applied after a price rise, while auctions often offer the most genuine value but need the most knowledge. First-time buyers are safest buying direct from a developer.

reasons.title: Developer discounts may follow a price rise
reasons.body: A unit priced at RM500,000 may be revised to RM600,000 and then offered at 10% off, which is close to where it started.

reasons.title: Agents step in when sales stall
reasons.body: Developers hand slow projects to agents who advertise aggressively online. Commissions are usually 2 to 3%, sometimes up to 7%; the harder a project is to sell, the higher it goes.

reasons.title: Group buys fill a building with investors
reasons.body: Gurus and clubs book blocks of units for members, with cash back of 15% up to 40% and an entry fee of a few thousand ringgit. A building full of investors and short stays can be unsettling for families who live there.

reasons.title: Auctions show the real value
reasons.body: When investors can't keep up their instalments, units go to auction at around 20 to 30% below market value, with the earlier gimmicks stripped out.

actions: Compare a discounted price with the price before any revision.
Get any agent's promises confirmed in writing in the agreement.
Before joining a club, check the entry fee and who else is buying in the block.
Learn the rules and process before bidding at auction.
If you're a first-time buyer, buy from an established developer.
caveat: Sean questions some cash-back practices; buying with multiple loans through such schemes is risky unless you know exactly what you are doing.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this June 2019 video. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
